topics.label: Course introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the lecture series, outlines key learning outcomes, and establishes the foundational questions and clinical relevance of cancer biology.

topics.label: Biological and architectural basis of cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: They describe cancer as a breakdown of normal cellular differentiation and tissue architecture driven by genetic and epigenetic alterations, alongside the challenges of modeling these processes in culture.

topics.label: Pathology and progression of tumor invasion and metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: They examine the histological features, anatomical routes, and stepwise pathological progression that distinguish local tissue invasion and distant metastasis from benign lesions.

topics.label: Tumor nomenclature and mechanisms of clinical morbidity
topics.groupedBecause: They establish the standard terminology for classifying neoplasms and explain the pathophysiological mechanisms through which both benign and malignant tumors cause patient morbidity and mortality.

topics.label: Cancer incidence and comparative oncology across species
topics.groupedBecause: They analyze epidemiological patterns of tumor frequency and mortality in humans and compare tumor incidence across diverse multicellular animal taxa.

topics.label: Principles and clinical methods of cancer screening
topics.groupedBecause: They discuss the clinical rationale for early cancer detection and evaluate specific screening approaches, diagnostic challenges, and outcomes across different tissue sites.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and practical preview
topics.groupedBecause: It concludes the lecture by reiterating the core learning outcomes and pointing forward to the upcoming practical sessions and future lectures.
